stemMd: Ethanol and dimethyl ether both have molecular formula C₂H₆O. How are they related?

options.label: B
options.textMd: They have different numbers of carbon atoms.

options.label: C
options.textMd: They are identical molecules under different names.

options.label: D
options.textMd: They must have identical physical properties.

options.label: E
options.textMd: They are structural isomers with different atom connectivity.

explanationMd: Structural isomers share a molecular formula but connect their atoms differently. Ethanol has a carbon-bound hydroxyl group; dimethyl ether has oxygen between two methyl groups. This change in connectivity produces different chemical and physical behaviour.

distractorRationale.a: Isotopes differ in neutron count, not molecular connectivity.
distractorRationale.c: An alcohol and an ether have different bonding arrangements.
distractorRationale.b: The common formula explicitly gives two carbons in each.
distractorRationale.d: Different functional groups can give different boiling points and interactions.
